name: Learn several useful mobility routines
blurb: Three short routines — a morning general one, a pre-training warm-up, and a desk-worker antidote for hips and thoracic spine — cover most of what an adult body needs.
gear: Optional: a foam roller and a resistance band
steps: Learn the difference between mobility (active control through range) and stretching (passive length). Mobility work is what actually transfers.
Build a 10-minute daily routine: cat-cow, thoracic rotations, 90/90 hip switches, deep squat holds, shoulder controlled articular rotations.
Build a pre-training warm-up specific to what you are about to do: wrists before handstands, hips before kicking, shoulders before pressing.
Build a desk-antidote sequence: hip flexor stretch, thoracic extension over a chair, chin tucks, wrist extensions.
Do them at fixed times attached to existing habits, and keep sessions short enough that you never skip them.
Retest a specific range monthly — deep squat depth, overhead reach — so you can see progress.
tips: Ten minutes daily beats an hour once a week by a wide margin.
Pain is not the goal. End range with control is.
proof: Thirty consecutive days of practice and a measurable improvement in at least one range of motion.
